name: present_files
description: Show files from your machine to the user, inline in this chat: images appear as pictures, videos as players, PDFs as documents, and any other file as a file the user can open or download. Use it when the user should see or receive a file you made or found, such as a chart, a screenshot, a rendered video, a PDF report, or an exported spreadsheet, including when the reader is not on this machine. Do not present text, code, or Markdown files; link them instead, because a link opens the live file in the viewer. Generated images, images you read with your file-reading tool, and artifacts are already shown when you make or read them, so do not present them again in the same chat. The files are copied when you call this, so later changes to them do not change what the user sees. An image may be at most 32 MiB, a video 256 MiB, and a document or other file 64 MiB, with at most 256 MiB per call. Optional layout: a small fragment of HTML with inline CSS (flexbox, grid, figure and figcaption) that arranges the files; each names one of filepaths exactly as you wrote it. Images show at their natural size unless you size them; width: 100% fills the width. Scripts, links, colours, and positioning are not supported; anything unsupported is ignored and reported back, and a file the layout leaves out is shown after it. Leave layout out and the chat arranges the files itself. For example:

filepaths.description: The files to show, in the order the user should see them

items.description: A file on your machine, absolute or relative to your working directory

layout.description: Optional small HTML fragment with inline CSS arranging the files; leave it out for the automatic layout
